critical_code_review_comments: server.py approve_deliverable: 'if d["client_id"] != client["id"] and client["role"] != "admin"' — this correctly lets admin approve on behalf of any client, but there is no audit trail of who approved. For a compliance-adjacent action, consider recording approver identity (approved_by_user_id / approved_at) rather than just setting status+updated_at.

sweep_overdue_invoices swallows all exceptions silently (except: pass). If the invoices table is renamed or the due_on column is missing, overdue flipping will silently fail and clients will see stale 'SENT' pills. Log the exception at WARN level.

sweep_overdue_invoices runs on EVERY /api/clients/ensure call (which happens on every login) and on every /api/admin/overview render. For a portal with growing invoice tables this is a full-table UPDATE with WHERE status='sent' AND due_on<today on every login — fine at demo scale, but at ~10k+ invoices consider a nightly cron or an index on (status, due_on).

Profile page uses supabase.from('clients').update(...).eq('id', profile.id) — relies entirely on RLS to prevent role escalation. Tested and safe today, but a defense-in-depth improvement would be to whitelist columns in RLS UPDATE policy (WITH CHECK role = OLD.role) rather than trusting the client to omit 'role' from the payload.

DeliverableDetail.approveCut only reads the top-level error.response.data.detail — if backend ever returns validation errors as a list (FastAPI 422), the user gets 'Approval failed' instead of the reason. Consider handling both string and list detail shapes.
